questions.title: ATM Light Command Terminal
questions.description:
A mini ATM kiosk prints a receipt line after every operation. Model the kiosk with an ATMLight class that keeps the balance private and exposes init(), deposit() and withdraw() member functions plus a printReceipt() member function for the closing summary. A deposit always succeeds and prints Deposit <amt>, balance <b>. A withdrawal larger than the current balance is declined and prints Withdraw <amt> declined, balance <b>; otherwise it prints Withdraw <amt>, balance <b>.
Read the starting balance and the number of commands N, then process N commands and finish with the receipt.

Input Format:
One line: starting balance (integer), N (integer), then N commands, each D or W followed by an amount.

Output Format:
One line per command as described above, then:
Final balance: <balance>

Constraints:
0 <= starting balance <= 100000, 1 <= N <= 8, 0 <= each amount <= 100000

questions.title: ATM Transaction Session
questions.description:
An ATM processes a session of withdrawal requests. The log starts with N (the number of records) and a starting balance B, followed by N record amounts processed in order with a do-while loop. An amount within the current balance is approved and deducted; anything larger is declined. A record equal to -1 means the session was cancelled: print the cancellation line and stop processing immediately, ignoring any remaining records.

Input Format:
First token: N. Second token: starting balance B. Then N integers, each an amount between 0 and 100000 or the cancel marker -1.

Output Format:
One line per processed record: TXN <i>: Approved, balance <new balance> or TXN <i>: Declined
When cancelled: Cancelled at record <i>
Processed: <number of records actually processed>
Final balance: <balance>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 50, 0 <= B <= 100000

questions.title: Abstract Employee Salary Desk
questions.description:
A payroll desk treats every worker as an Employee but pays them differently. The abstract Employee class declares pure virtual salary(); a Manager adds a bonus to a fixed base, a Worker multiplies hourly rate by hours worked. Read the employee code, create the right object through an Employee pointer and print the computed salary.

Input Format:
One line starting with a character: M followed by base and bonus, or W followed by rate and hours (all integers).

Output Format:
Salary: <computed salary>

Constraints:
1 <= each value <= 1000000; code is M or W.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= each value <= 1000000; code is M or W

questions.title: Abstract Machine Work Report
questions.description:
An abstract class can mix ready-made behaviour with pure contracts. Machine provides the concrete method ready() that prints 'Machine ready', while work() stays pure virtual. Printer and Scanner complete the contract with their own work lines. Read the machine code and unit number, then print both the shared concrete step and the derived step.

Input Format:
One line with a character (P for printer, S for scanner) and an integer unit number.

Output Format:
Machine ready
<work line> on unit <unit>   (Printing job for P, Scanning page for S)

Constraints:
Code is P or S; 1 <= unit <= 1000.
questions.inputconstrains: Code is P or S; 1 <= unit <= 1000

questions.title: Account Deposit Validator
questions.description:
A bank backend rejects negative deposits before they ever touch a balance. Define a class Account with private holder and balance, setHolder() and setBalance() setters, a deposit() member function that returns false and changes nothing when the amount is negative (accepted otherwise) and a getBalance() getter. Read the holder, the opening balance and three deposit attempts, then report each attempt and the final balance.

Input Format:
One line with five tokens: holder (single word), opening balance (integer) and three deposit amounts (integers).

Output Format:
Holder: <holder>
Deposit <amount>: Accepted or Deposit <amount>: Rejected (three lines, in order)
Final balance: <balance after the accepted deposits>

Constraints:
0 <= opening balance <= 100000, -1000 <= each amount <= 100000

questions.title: Add Two Numbers Function
questions.description:
Modular programs start with tiny reusable units. Define a function int add(int a, int b) that receives two integers as parameters and returns their sum. Read the two integers in main and print the result by calling the function.

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b.

Output Format:
Sum: <a + b>

Constraints:
-1000 <= a, b <= 1000

questions.title: Age Group Classifier
questions.description:
A vaccination drive sorts visitors into age groups. Read the age (integer) and print the group using an else-if ladder: below 13 Child, 13 to 19 Teen, 20 to 59 Adult, 60 and above Senior.

Input Format:
One line with one integer A.

Output Format:
Age: <A>
Group: Child (A < 13), Teen (13 to 19), Adult (20 to 59), Senior (60 and above)

Constraints:
1 <= A <= 120

questions.title: Alert Broadcast Interface
questions.description:
A monitoring hub broadcasts alerts through a notification interface. Notifier declares pure virtual send(msg) and nothing else; EmailAlert prints an EMAIL line and SMSAlert prints an SMS line. Read the channel code, then the whole message line (it may contain spaces), and dispatch polymorphically through the interface pointer.

Input Format:
First a character (E for email, S for SMS), then after one space (or on the next line) the message text.

Output Format:
EMAIL: <message>
or
SMS: <message>

Constraints:
Code is E or S; 1 <= message length <= 60.
questions.inputconstrains: Code is E or S; 1 <= message length <= 60

questions.title: Anagram Pair Checker
questions.description:
A puzzle app checks whether two words use exactly the same letters with the same counts, ignoring case. Read two words and print whether they are anagrams.

Input Format:
One line with two words separated by a space (English letters only).

Output Format:
Anagrams
or
Not anagrams

Constraints:
1 <= each word length <= 100
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= each word length <= 100, English letters only

questions.description:
A pet simulator uses single inheritance: class Dog derives from class Animal and gains everything Animal has. Animal offers eat() and Dog adds bark(). Write the program so main creates a Dog object and prints both inherited and new behaviour.

Input Format:
No input.

Output Format:
Animal eats food
Dog barks loudly

Constraints:
None.

questions.title: Animal Sounds via Pure Virtual
questions.description:
Every pet answers differently, yet the kennel desk treats them all as one type. Animal declares a pure virtual speak(); Dog and Cat each override it with their own sound. Read the pet code and name, create the matching animal through an Animal pointer, and make it speak polymorphically.

Input Format:
One line with a character (D for dog, C for cat) and the pet's name (single word).

Output Format:
<name> says <sound>   (Dog says Woof, Cat says Meow)

Constraints:
Code is D or C; 1 <= name length <= 20.
questions.inputconstrains: Code is D or C; 1 <= name length <= 20

questions.title: Append Note Builder
questions.description:
A sticky-notes tool keeps one note per line in app20.txt. The program always starts the file with the base line 'Notes started' and then appends the note typed by the user using append mode. Finally it prints every line of the finished file.

Input Format:
One line of text (the user note; may contain spaces).

Output Format:
Every line of app20.txt after the append, in order (the base line first, then the user note).

Constraints:
1 <= note length <= 60
questions.output3:
Notes started
last note of the day

questions.title: Append Versus Overwrite Demo
questions.description:
A mode tester shows what out mode and append mode do to the same file. It first plants old content in mode20.txt, then reopens the file in plain out mode with the first input word (erasing what was there), appends the second word, and finally appends the third word. After every step the whole file is read back and printed, so the mode effects are visible.

Input Format:
One line with three words separated by spaces.

Output Format:
After overwrite: <file content after the out-mode write>
After append: <content after appending the second word>
Final content: <content after appending the third word>

Constraints:
Each word is 1 to 12 characters.

questions.title: Array Element Sum Drill
questions.description:
A cashier totals the day's transactions stored in a list. Read N and then N integers into an array, add them up while traversing the array and print the total.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N array elements.

Output Format:
Sum: <total>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= element <= 10000

questions.title: Array Tour with a Moving Pointer
questions.description:
A projector operator walks through a slide deck using a pointer. Read N integers into an array, then traverse it with a pointer using p++ and *(p + i), printing all values on one line separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
First line: one integer N.
Second line: N integers.

Output Format:
Values: <v1> <v2> ... <vN>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, -1000 <= each value <= 1000

questions.title: Assembly Line Grid Multiplier
questions.description:
An assembly plant tracks items moving through stages; the stage-count grid (R1 x C1) is multiplied by the routing-weight grid (R2 x C2) to compute line totals. The two matrices are always compatible for multiplication (C1 = R2 guaranteed). Read the dimensions and both grids, echo the dimensions, then print the product matrix.

Input Format:
First line: R1 and C1.
Second line: R2 and C2 (C1 = R2 guaranteed).
Then: R1*C1 integers (matrix A) in row-major order.
Then: R2*C2 integers (matrix B) in row-major order.

Output Format:
A size: <R1>x<C1>
B size: <R2>x<C2>
Result size: <R1>x<C2>
Then R1 lines with the product matrix, values separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= R1, C1, R2, C2 <= 50, C1 = R2, -1000 <= element <= 1000

questions.title: Attendance Register Count
questions.description:
A class teacher marks the register as a list of 0s and 1s, one value per student (1 = present, 0 = absent). Read N and then N attendance values into an array, then count how many students are present and how many are absent.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N attendance values (each 0 or 1).

Output Format:
Present: <count of 1s>
Absent: <count of 0s>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, each value is 0 or 1

questions.title: Auction Runner-up Bid
questions.description:
An auction house recorded N bids. The highest bid wins; the runner-up is the highest bid that is strictly lower than the winning bid. Read N and then N bids into an array, then report both values.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N bids.

Output Format:
Highest bid: <maximum>
Runner-up bid: <second highest distinct value>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= bid <= 100000, at least two distinct bid values exist
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= bid <= 100000, at least two distinct bid values exist

questions.title: Audit Trail Session Logger
questions.description:
A security tool writes one audit file across three sessions. For session 1 it opens audit20.txt in plain out mode (fresh start); sessions 2 and 3 open the same file in append mode. Each session writes the header 'Session k' followed by k entry words, one per line. Read the three sessions from input, write them, then reopen the file and print the complete audit trail with line numbers and the total line count.

Input Format:
One line with three session descriptions: k1 entry... k2 entry... k3 entry... (each session starts with its entry count followed by that many single-word entries).

Output Format:
One numbered line per file line: <i>: <line>
Then: Total lines: <count>

Constraints:
0 <= entries per session <= 3; each entry is a single word of 1 to 12 characters

questions.title: Backup Folder Size Sum
questions.description:
A backup tool inspects a folder holding N files and totals their sizes recursively: every call reads one size into the running total and then recurses on the rest. Read N and then N sizes, and print the folder report.

Input Format:
First line: N. Second line: N integers (sizes in MB).

Output Format:
Files: <N>
Total size: <total> MB

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= each size <= 5000

questions.title: Ballot Frequency Report
questions.description:
An electronic ballot box logged N votes as candidate IDs between 0 and 100. Read N and then N votes into an array, then produce the tally: print every distinct candidate ID in the order it was first seen, each with the number of votes it received.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N candidate IDs.

Output Format:
For each distinct ID in first-seen order, one line:
Candidate <id>: <votes>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= candidate ID <= 100

questions.title: Bank Account Opening
questions.description:
A bank console opens an account as an object built from customer data. Define a class BankAccount with a parameterized constructor that takes the holder name (single word) and the opening balance (a double) and stores them, plus a display() function that prints the account details with the balance shown to exactly two decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: holder name (single word) and balance (a double).

Output Format:
Account opened
Holder: <holder>
Balance: <balance with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0 <= balance <= 1000000

questions.title: Bank Account Statement Class
questions.description:

Input Format:
One line with three tokens: owner (single word), starting balance (integer) and deposit amount (integer).

Output Format:
Owner: <owner>
Start balance: <start>
Deposit: <amount>
Final balance: <start + amount>

Constraints:
0 <= starting balance <= 100000, 0 <= deposit <= 100000

questions.title: Bank Ledger Statement Builder
questions.description:
A mini banking app records every transaction in ledger20.txt with the running balance. Read N and then N transactions (a character D for deposit or W for withdrawal, followed by an integer amount). The balance starts at 0. For each transaction write a line 'type amount Balance: <new balance>' to the file. Then reopen the file, read it line by line, parse every line to recover the amount and the running balance, print the full statement, and finally report the final balance and the largest single transaction amount, both computed from the file.

Input Format:
First line: N. Then N lines, each with a character (D or W) and an integer amount.

Output Format:
One statement line per transaction exactly as stored.
Then: Final balance: <balance parsed from the last line>
Largest transaction: <largest amount parsed from the file>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 20, 1 <= amount <= 10000; the balance may go negative

questions.title: Bank Transaction Classifier
questions.description:
A bank teller terminal classifies each transaction and computes fees through one function. Read two transactions (type and amount each), classify both and print a receipt with the total fees.

Input Format:
One line with four tokens: type1 (D or W), amount1, type2 (D or W), amount2.

TXN 1: <label> of <amount, 2 decimals> (Fee: <fee, 2 decimals>)
TXN 2: <label> of <amount, 2 decimals> (Fee: <fee, 2 decimals>)
Total fees: <sum of fees, 2 decimals>

1 <= each amount <= 1000000, type is D or W

questions.title: Bank Transfer Validator
questions.description:
A banking backend validates transfers with two custom exception classes, both deriving from std::exception and overriding what(): InvalidAccount (message Invalid account number) and InsufficientFunds (message Insufficient funds). Read the balance, the account number and the amount. Inside a try block: an account outside 100000 to 999999 throws InvalidAccount; an amount greater than the balance throws InsufficientFunds; otherwise print the success line. Catch each exception type in its own handler, each printing Transfer failed: followed by what().

Input Format:
One line with three integers: balance, account, amount.

Output Format:
Transfer of <amount> to account <account> completed
or:
Transfer failed: Invalid account number
or:
Transfer failed: Insufficient funds

Constraints:
0 <= balance <= 1000000, 0 <= account <= 2000000, 0 <= amount <= 1000000
questions.whitelist: class, exception, what, try, catch, throw

Read a duty code and an employee name, create the matching derived object through a base pointer, bind a Staff reference to it, and call role().

One line with a character and a word: 'M' for Manager, 'D' for Developer, and the employee name.

Output Format:
Badge: <name>
Manager on duty      (code M)
or
Developer on duty    (code D)

Constraints:
Code is 'M' or 'D'; name is one word of at most 20 letters.

Output Format:
One line per cycle: Cycle <i>: <remaining>%

Final charge: <remaining>%

Constraints:
0 <= T < P <= 100, 1 <= R <= 100

questions.title: Big Integer Adder with Operator+
questions.description:
Cryptography utilities often need arithmetic beyond 64-bit. Define a BigInt class that stores a non-negative decimal number as a string of digits (up to 40 digits) and overloads the + operator to perform school-book addition from the least significant digit with carries. Read two big integers, echo them and print the sum with no leading zeros.

One line with two decimal strings a and b (no leading zeros, length 1 to 40 each).

Output Format:
Line 1: 'A: <a>'.
Line 2: 'B: <b>'.
Line 3: 'Sum: <a + b>' with leading zeros removed (a sum of zero prints as 0).

Constraints:
1 <= length <= 40 digits, both values are non-negative

questions.title: Binary Beacon Triangle
questions.description:
A drone show arranges beacons in a triangle. The beacon in row i, column j glows (prints 1) when (i + j) % 2 equals 1 and stays dark (prints 0) otherwise. Read an integer N and print N rows; row i contains i digits separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
One line with one integer N.

Output Format:
N lines; row i has i digits (0 or 1) separated by single spaces; the digit in row i, column j is (i + j) % 2.
For sample input 4 the display is:
0
1 0
0 1 0
1 0 1 0

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 15

questions.title: Bitwise Trio Probe
questions.description:
Bitwise operators work on the individual bits of two integers. Read two non-negative integers a and b (each below 16) and print the results of bitwise AND, bitwise OR and bitwise XOR.

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b.

Output Format:
AND: <a & b>
OR: <a | b>
XOR: <a ^ b>

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 15

questions.title: Blood Donation Eligibility Desk
questions.description:
A blood bank kiosk screens walk-in donors with three gates applied in order: age first, then weight, then gap since the last donation. Read the age, the weight in kg and the number of days since the last donation. A donor is eligible only when age is between 18 and 65 (inclusive), weight is at least 50 kg and the last donation was 90 or more days ago. Use nested if statements so the first failed gate decides the rejection reason: under age, over age, under weight or recent donation.

Input Format:
One line with three integers: age, weight, days since last donation.

Output Format:
Age: <age>
Weight: <weight>
Last donation: <days> days ago
Status: Eligible (all gates pass) or Status: Rejected - under age | over age | under weight | recent donation

Constraints:
1 <= age <= 100, 1 <= weight <= 200, 0 <= days <= 2000

questions.description:
A library system derives Book from LibraryItem. The inherited registration line is printed, then the book's borrow report: title, total copies, borrowed count and the copies still available.

Input Format:
One line with a title (single word) and two integers: total copies and borrowed count.

Output Format:
Item registered in library
Book: <title>
Total copies: <copies>
Borrowed: <borrowed>
Available: <copies - borrowed>

1 <= copies <= 500, 0 <= borrowed <= copies

questions.title: Book Details Class
questions.description:
A library catalogue lists every book as an object. Define a class Book with a public title (string) and pages (int), read them, and call its printDetails() member function.

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: title (single word) and pages (integer).

Output Format:
Title: <title>
Pages: <pages>

Constraints:
1 <= pages <= 2000

questions.title: Box Constructor Selector
questions.description:
A packaging unit builds boxes with three overloaded constructors: a default constructor for a 1 x 1 x 1 box, a one-argument constructor for a cube, and a two-argument constructor for a flat box whose height is fixed at 1. Each constructor prints a line announcing which one was used. Read a mode k and the matching dimensions, construct exactly one Box object, then print its volume.

Input Format:
The first integer k is the constructor mode: 0, 1 or 2. If k is 1, one more integer s (side) follows. If k is 2, two more integers l and w follow. If k is 0, nothing follows.

Output Format:
For k=0: Default constructor: 1 x 1 x 1 then Volume: 1
For k=1: Cube constructor: <s> x <s> x <s> then Volume: <s*s*s>
For k=2: Box constructor: <l> x <w> x 1 then Volume: <l*w>

Constraints:
k is 0, 1 or 2; 1 <= s, l, w <= 100

questions.title: Box Set and Show
questions.description:
A packaging app models every parcel as a Box object. Define a class Box with a private side, a setSide() setter, a getSide() getter and a show() member function. Read the side, store it through the setter and call show().

Input Format:
One line with one integer: side.

Output Format:
Box side: <side>
Volume: <side * side * side>

Constraints:
1 <= side <= 50

questions.title: Box Template Holds a Value
questions.description:
A class template Box<T> stores exactly one value of any type. Define the template with a constructor and a get() method, then instantiate it twice: Box<int> from an integer input and Box<double> from a double input.

Input Format:
Line 1: one integer.
Line 2: one double.

Output Format:
Int box holds: <the integer>
Double box holds: <the double, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
-100000 <= integer <= 100000, -100000.0 <= double <= 100000.0

questions.title: Butterfly Wing LED Wall
questions.description:
A butterfly garden builds an LED wall of two mirrored star wings. Read an integer N and print 2N - 1 rows. Upper rows i = 1 to N: print i stars with no separator, then 2 * (N - i) spaces, then i stars again with no separator. Lower rows: repeat the same rule for i from N - 1 down to 1. The middle row (i = N) has no gap, so both wings join into 2N stars.

Input Format:
One line with one integer N.

Output Format:
2N - 1 lines forming a butterfly.
For sample input 4 the wall is:
*      *
**    **
***  ***
********
***  ***
**    **
*      *

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 10

questions.title: By-Value Argument Copy Trace

Define a class Counter with a parameterized constructor printing 'Created counter <v>', a copy constructor printing 'Copied counter <v>', a destructor printing 'Destroyed counter <v>', and a show() function printing 'Value: <v>'. Read v, build the Counter, then call a function that takes the Counter by value twice, and finally print 'Done'.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: v.

Output Format:
Created counter <v>
Copied counter <v>
Value: <v>
Destroyed counter <v>
Copied counter <v>
Value: <v>
Destroyed counter <v>
Done
Destroyed counter <v>

Constraints:
1 <= v <= 100

questions.title: CSV Record Formatter
questions.description:
A legacy HR export stores one record per line as name,department,score with exactly two commas. Read the whole line with getline, split it manually on the commas (no split libraries), and print the three parsed fields, followed by a padded table row: the name padded with trailing spaces to width 10, the department padded to width 12, and the score right-aligned in width 5, all between | characters.

Input Format:
One line: name,department,score (name and department contain no commas; score is an integer).

Output Format:
Name: <name>
Department: <dept>
Score: <score>
Row: |<name width 10>|<dept width 12>|<score width 5 right-aligned>|

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 10, 1 <= department length <= 12, 0 <= score <= 100

questions.title: Caesar Cipher Engine
questions.description:
A secret club encodes messages with a Caesar cipher. Read a word and a shift K. Shift every letter forward by K positions in the alphabet, wrapping around from z to a (and Z to A) while preserving case. Print the plain word, the cipher text, and the cipher text reversed.

Input Format:
One line with a word (English letters only) and an integer K separated by a space.

Output Format:
Plain: <word>
Cipher: <shifted word>
Backwards: <reversed cipher>

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 50, 0 <= K <= 25

questions.title: Cafe Tip Calculator
questions.description:
A cafe app adds a tip before settling the bill. Read the bill amount (double rupees) and the tip percentage (integer). Print the tip amount and the total, both with two decimal places, plus the whole-rupee total obtained by truncating the decimals.

Input Format:
One line with a double and an integer: bill amount, tip percent.

Output Format:
Tip: <tip, 2 decimals>
Total: <bill + tip, 2 decimals>
Whole rupees: <integer part of total>

Constraints:
1 <= bill <= 100000, 0 <= tip percent <= 50

questions.title: Cafeteria Bill
questions.description:
The college cafeteria charges per plate. Read the price of one plate (integer rupees) and the number of plates ordered (integer). Print the bill with a 5 rupee packing charge added once.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: plate price and plate count.

Output Format:
Food total: <price * count>
Packing: 5
Bill: <price * count + 5>

Constraints:
1 <= plate price <= 500, 1 <= plate count <= 100

questions.title: Calendar Advancer with Increment Operators
questions.description:
A calendar service steps through dates one day at a time. Define a Date class and overload both ++ operators: prefix (++d) and postfix (d++) must each advance the date by one day, handling month lengths (30, 31, 28) and leap-year Februaries (years divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400), rolling over months and years. Read a start date and N, then print the sequence of N+1 dates, advancing with prefix ++ on odd steps and postfix ++ on even steps.

Input Format:
One line with four integers: dd mm yyyy n (the start date is a valid calendar date).

Output Format:
N+1 lines, each 'dd-mm-yyyy' with dd and mm shown as exactly two digits (zero padded), starting with the given date and then every advanced date.

Constraints:
1900 <= yyyy <= 2100, 1 <= n <= 60

questions.title: Campus Registry Console
questions.description:
A university registry runs on hierarchical inheritance: Person branches into Student and Professor. The console reads a count and then that many commands; each command starts with the word student or professor, followed by a name and a value (marks for students, publication count for professors). Students print a grade (PASS at 40 marks or more, otherwise FAIL) and professors print a status (ACTIVE at 5 publications or more, otherwise RISING).

Input Format:
First line: integer n.
Next n lines: <kind> <name> <value> where kind is student or professor.

Output Format:
For each entry in input order:
STUDENT <name> marks <value> grade <PASS or FAIL>
PROFESSOR <name> publications <value> status <ACTIVE or RISING>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, 0 <= marks, publications <= 100

Mileage: <distance / fuel> km per litre

questions.title: Car Showroom Info Class
questions.description:
A showroom lists cars as objects. Define a class Car with a private brand (string) and speed (int), setters for both and a showInfo() member function. Read the brand and top speed, store them and call showInfo().

Output Format:
Brand: <brand>
Top speed: <speed> km/h

40 <= speed <= 300

questions.title: Card Number Query Pipeline
questions.description:
A library issues card numbers, sometimes with re-issues that create duplicates. Read N card numbers, build a sorted list of distinct numbers using sort followed by unique (with erase), and answer Q queries. For each query value, use lower_bound: print Position <i> (0-based index in the distinct list) if the value exists, otherwise print absent.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N integers (card numbers, duplicates possible).
Line 3: integer Q.
Line 4: Q query values.

Output Format:
First line: Unique cards: <number of distinct values>
For each query in order: Position <0-based index> or absent

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= Q <= 500, -100000 <= value <= 100000

questions.title: Case Toggle Transformer
questions.description:
A chat app has a playful toggle mode that flips the case of every letter: lowercase becomes uppercase and uppercase becomes lowercase. Read one word and print the flipped version. Non-letter characters stay unchanged.

Input Format:
One line with one word (letters and digits).

Output Format:
Toggled: <flipped word>

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 100

questions.title: Case-Blind Palindrome Checker
questions.description:
A quality team checks product tags that must read the same forwards and backwards, ignoring letter case. Read one word, compare it with its reverse case-insensitively, and print the verdict.

Input Format:
One line with one word (English letters only).

Output Format:
Palindrome
or
Not a palindrome

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 100

questions.title: Cash Machine Withdrawal Guard
questions.description:
An ATM processes a withdrawal inside a try block. Read the account balance and the withdrawal amount. If the amount exceeds the balance, throw runtime_error with the message Insufficient balance, and the catch handler prints the failure line. Otherwise the withdrawal succeeds and the remaining balance is shown.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: balance and amount.

Output Format:
Withdrawal successful
Remaining balance: <balance - amount>
or:
Withdrawal failed: Insufficient balance

Constraints:
0 <= balance <= 1000000, 0 <= amount <= 1000000

questions.title: Centered Stage Pyramid
questions.description:
A concert stage arranges spotlights in a centered pyramid. Read an integer N and print N rows; row i (1-based) begins with N - i leading spaces and then prints i stars separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
One line with one integer N.

Output Format:
N lines; row i has N - i leading spaces followed by i stars separated by single spaces.

   *
  * *
 * * *
* * * *

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 15

questions.title: Character Echo Box
questions.description:
Computers store characters as numbers. Read a single character and print it together with its integer (ASCII) code and the character that follows it in the ASCII table.

Input Format:
One line with one character.

Output Format:
Char: <c>
Code: <ascii value>
Next: <c + 1 as character>

Constraints:
Input character is a printable ASCII character (code 33 to 125).

questions.title: Chat Word Frequency Report
questions.description:
A chat analytics dashboard counts how often each word appears in a message batch. Read N words and tally them in a map<string, int>. Print every word with its count in alphabetical order of the word.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N words separated by spaces.

Output Format:
For every distinct word in alphabetical order: <word> <count>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, each word has at most 20 letters, comparison is case sensitive (ok and OK differ)

Input Format:
One line with a character (C for card, U for UPI) and an integer amount.

Output Format:
Payable: <amount returned by charge>

Constraints:
100 <= amount <= 1000000; code is C or U.

questions.title: Cinema Checkerboard Occupancy Map
questions.description:
A cinema control panel stores the occupancy map of a hall in a 2D character array before printing it. Read R (rows) and C (seats per row); seat (i, j) is occupied when (i + j) % 2 equals 0 and prints 'X', otherwise it is free and prints '-'. Store the characters in a 2D array first, then print the map row by row with no separator between seats.

Input Format:
One line with two integers R and C.

Output Format:
R lines of C characters each ('X' or '-'), forming a checkerboard.

X-X-
-X-X
X-X-

1 <= R, C <= 12

questions.title: Circle Area Function Drill
questions.description:
A drafting office needs circle areas all day long. Define a function double areaOfCircle(double radius) that receives the radius as a parameter and returns the area computed with PI = 3.14159. Read the radius (a double) in main and print the radius and the area (two decimal places) returned by the function.

Input Format:
One line with one double: radius.

Output Format:
Radius: <radius>
Area: <PI * r * r with 2 decimals>

0.1 <= radius <= 1000

questions.title: Circle Area with Constant PI
questions.description:
Declare a constant PI = 3.14159 and use it to compute the area of a circle. Read the radius (an integer) and print the area rounded down to the nearest whole square unit.

One line with one integer: radius.

Output Format:
Exact area: <PI * r * r>
Whole area: <integer part of the area>

Constraints:
1 <= radius <= 1000

questions.title: Circle Radius Gate Class
questions.description:
A geometry engine guards its Circle objects: only positive radii may be stored. Define a class Circle with a private radius and a private hasRadius flag, an init() member function that clears both, a setRadius() member function that returns false and stores nothing when the value is 0 or negative (accepted otherwise), an area() member function using 3.14159 and a ready() member function telling whether a valid radius was set. One line with three integers: three candidate radii.

Radius <r>: Accepted or Radius <r>: Rejected (three lines, in order)

Area: <3.14159 * radius * radius, 2 decimals>
or, when every candidate was rejected:
No valid radius

-100 <= each radius <= 1000

A smart bulb changes state every time it is toggled. XOR-ing the state bit with 1 flips it, and doing that an even number of times brings it back to the start. Read the initial state (0 or 1) and the number of toggles, then report the final state using bitwise XOR.

One line with two integers: initial state (0 or 1) and number of toggles.

Output Format:

Toggles: <k>
After: <state ^ (k % 2)>

0 <= state <= 1, 0 <= k <= 100

0 <= metres <= 1000, 0 <= cm <= 99; for '-' the first distance is never smaller than the second

A civil drafting student measures a rectangular plot. Read the width and height in metres (integers) and print the area and the perimeter.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: width and height.

Output Format:
Area: <width * height>
Perimeter: <2 * (width + height)>

Constraints:
1 <= width, height <= 10000

questions.title: Rectangle Class Area
questions.description:
A drafting tool stores shapes as objects. Define a class Rectangle with public width and height, read both from input, and let a member function print the dimensions and call the area() member function for the area.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: width and height.

Output Format:
Rectangle <width>x<height>
Area: <width * height>

Constraints:
1 <= width, height <= 1000

questions.title: Recursive Descending List
questions.description:
A launchpad test bench prints its test indices in reverse order as a recursion warm-up. Read N and print the numbers from N down to 1 on a single line separated by single spaces, using a recursive function.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
One line with N, N-1, ..., 1 separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000

questions.title: Recursive Digit Counter
questions.description:
A water meter portal counts how many digits a reading contains using recursion: each call strips the last digit and adds 1, and any single-digit number (including 0) counts as 1 digit. Read N and print the count.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Digit count: <c>

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 1000000

questions.title: Recursive Factorial Finder
questions.description:
A chemistry lab counts possible arrangements of sample trays and needs factorials computed by recursion: N! = N * (N-1)!, stopping at 0! = 1. Read N and print N! using a function that calls itself.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Factorial of <N> is <result>

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 15

questions.title: Recursive Kitchen Timer
questions.description:
A smart kitchen timer ticks second by second with recursion, showing the remaining time in minutes:seconds form (seconds always shown as two digits) until it reaches zero. Read the total seconds S and print the full tick trace.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: S.

Output Format:
Timer set
Time left: <m>:<ss>   (one line per remaining second, from S down to 1)
Time up: 00:00

Constraints:
0 <= S <= 300

questions.title: Recursive Power of X
questions.description:
An embedded systems lab computes sensor scaling factors x^n with a recursive power function that multiplies the base n times and returns 1 when the exponent hits 0. Read the base and the exponent.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: base x and exponent n.

Output Format:
Power result: <x^n>

Constraints:
1 <= x <= 9, 0 <= n <= 15

questions.title: Recursive Sum to N
questions.description:
A maths mentor app builds a warm-up drill where the running total of all points from 1 to N is produced by a function that calls itself with N-1 until it reaches 0. Read N and print the recursive total. The core logic must use recursion, not loops.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Sum 1..N is <total>

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 1000

questions.title: Reference Swap Helper
questions.description:
Call by reference gives a function real power over the caller's variables. Read two integers, print them, then call void swapVals(int& a, int& b) which exchanges the two integers through reference parameters. Print the values again after the call to show that the change survived outside the function.

Input Format:
One line with two integers x and y.

Output Format:
Before: <x> <y>
After: <y> <x>

Constraints:
-100000 <= x, y <= 100000

questions.title: Referral Bonus Waterfall
questions.description:
A startup runs a referral bonus waterfall along a management chain: level 1 is the bottom employee and level N is the top. Level 1 receives its own bonus; every higher level k receives its own bonus plus double the payout of the level below: payout(k) = bonus(k) + 2 * payout(k-1). Read N and the N bonuses (level 1 first) with recursion, then print every level's payout and the top payout, all computed recursively. Input Format: First line: N. Second line: N integers (bonuses from level 1 to level N). Output Format: Chain length: Level 1 payout:

Level 2 payout:

... Level payout:

Top payout:

Constraints: 1 <= N <= 10, 0 <= each bonus <= 9

questions.title: Relational Signal Board
questions.description:
A robot controller converts sensor comparisons into signal bits. Read two integers a and b and print the results of four relational comparisons, each displayed as 1 for true or 0 for false.

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b.

Output Format:
A > B: <1 or 0>
A < B: <1 or 0>
A == B: <1 or 0>
A != B: <1 or 0>

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 100

Output Format: For each job in input order: === Report: === Text job: TEXT header for <title> TEXT body lines TEXT footer signature Html job: <h1><title></h1> <p>report body</p> <small>generated by atom</small> Both end with: === End of report === Constraints: 1 <= N <= 20; title is one word of at most 20 letters.

questions.title: Reverse the Digits of a Number
questions.description:
A mirror-lock app unlocks when the user types the reverse of a code number. Read a non-negative integer and print its digits reversed as a number (reversing 1200 gives 21 because leading zeros disappear).

Input Format:
One line with one non-negative integer.

Output Format:
Reversed: <reversed number>

Constraints:
0 <= number <= 2000000000

questions.title: Robot Arm Tower of Hanoi
questions.description:
A museum robot arm rearranges a tower of N disks on three pegs A, B and C, moving the whole stack from A to C under the classic rules: one disk per move and never a bigger disk on a smaller one. Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Disk count: <N>
Minimum moves: <2^N - 1>
Move disk <k> from <peg> to <peg>   (one line per move, in order)
All disks stacked on peg C

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 4. With N = 0 there are no moves and only the opening lines and the final line print.

questions.title: Rocket Altitude Precedence Trace
questions.description:
A rocketry club validates the classic height formula h = v0 * t - g / 2 * t * t with g = 10 before trusting its flight computer. Because C++ evaluates * and / before - and resolves same-precedence operators left to right, the expression g / 2 * t * t means ((g / 2) * t) * t. Read the launch speed v0 and the flight time t (integers), print every intermediate step exactly as computed, then classify the flight and print the theoretical apex height v0 * v0 / 20 as a double with two decimals.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: v0 and t.

Output Format:
v0: <v0>
t: <t>
Step 1 (v0 * t): <product>
Step 2 (t * t): <square>
Step 3 (g / 2 * t * t): <10 / 2 * t * t>
Step 4 (height): <step1 - step3>
Status: <AIRBORNE when height > 0, LAUNCH POINT when height == 0, LANDED when height < 0>
Apex height: <v0 * v0 / 20.0, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0 <= v0 <= 500, 0 <= t <= 60

questions.title: Rocket Countdown Liftoff
questions.description:
A college space club simulator fires a rocket with a recursive countdown: each call prints its own count and then calls itself with one less, until the base case prints the launch call. Read the starting count N and print the countdown.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
One number per line from N down to 1, then the line Liftoff!

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 30

questions.title: Roll Number Finder
questions.description:
During a surprise audit a teacher searches the roll list for a particular roll number. Read N, then N roll numbers into an array, then the target roll number. Search the array from the start; if the target appears, print the position of its first occurrence using 1-based numbering, otherwise print Not Found.

Input Format:
One line with N + 2 integers: N, the N roll numbers, then the target roll number.

Output Format:
Found at position <1-based position of the first occurrence>
or
Not Found

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= roll number <= 9999

questions.title: Run-Length Text Compressor
questions.description:
A log shipper shrinks text by replacing each run of repeated letters with the letter followed by the run length. Read one lowercase word and print its compressed form. Example: aaabb becomes a3b2 and a single letter becomes a1.

Input Format:
One line with one word of lowercase letters.

Output Format:
Compressed: <compressed form>

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 60

questions.title: Runtime Type Code Switch
questions.description:
A device dock asks every gadget for its runtime type code and switches on the answer. Base Device declares virtual typeCode() returning 0; Laptop, Phone and Tablet override it to return 1, 2 and 3 and store their charge hours. Read N devices, park them in an array of Device pointers, then loop, call typeCode() polymorphically, and switch on the returned code to print the device line.

Input Format:
First line: N. Next N lines: a character ('L' laptop, 'P' phone, 'T' tablet) and an integer hours.

Output Format:
For each device in input order, according to its runtime code:
Laptop charged <hours> hours
Phone charged <hours> hours
Tablet charged <hours> hours

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 50; 1 <= hours <= 24.

questions.title: SKU Code Formatter
questions.description:
A catalogue system formats product codes by attaching the code length. Read the product code (a single word) and print it followed by a dash and its length.

Input Format:
One line with one word: the product code.

Output Format:
Code: <code>-<length>

Constraints:
1 <= code length <= 30

questions.title: Safe Divider Drill
questions.description:
A math lab drills guarded division. Read two integers a and b. Inside a try block, print the quotient and the remainder when b is not zero; when b is zero, throw an exception so the catch handler prints the error line.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: a and b.

Output Format:
Quotient: <a / b>
Remainder: <a % b>
or, when b is zero:
Cannot divide by zero

Constraints:
-1000 <= a <= 1000, -100 <= b <= 100

questions.title: SalaryGuard Custom Exception
questions.description:
The payroll service validates salaries with its own exception type. Define a class SalaryError that derives publicly from std::exception, stores a message and overrides what() to return it. Read one integer salary. Inside a try block: a salary of zero or less throws SalaryError with the message Salary must be positive; a salary above 1000000 throws SalaryError with the message Salary exceeds maximum; otherwise print the acceptance line. The catch(const SalaryError&) handler prints SalaryError: followed by what().

Input Format:
One line with one integer: salary.

Output Format:
Salary accepted: <salary>
or:
SalaryError: <message from what()>

Constraints:
-100000 <= salary <= 2000000

questions.title: Sand Timer Hourglass Display
questions.description:
A meditation app shows a star hourglass: an inverted pyramid stacked on a pyramid. Read an integer N and print 2N - 1 rows.
The upper part has N rows: row i (1-based) begins with i - 1 leading spaces and then prints N - i + 1 stars separated by single spaces.
The lower part has N - 1 rows: for i from 2 to N, print N - i leading spaces followed by i stars separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
One line with one integer N.

Output Format:
2N - 1 lines forming the hourglass as specified above.
For sample input 3 the hourglass is:
* * *
 * *
  *
 * *
* * *

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 15

questions.title: Scholarship Eligibility Check
questions.description:
The scholarship cell applies one combined rule: a student is eligible only when marks are at least 80 AND attendance is at least 75 percent. Read the marks and the attendance percent and print each condition separately plus the combined decision, every result shown as 1 or 0.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: marks and attendance percent.

Output Format:
Marks OK: <marks >= 80 as 1 or 0>
Attendance OK: <attendance >= 75 as 1 or 0>
Eligible: <marks >= 80 && attendance >= 75 as 1 or 0>

Constraints:
0 <= marks <= 100, 0 <= attendance <= 100

questions.title: Score Card with Subscript Operator
questions.description:
A quiz platform stores five component marks for a contestant. Define a Score class that keeps the marks in an array and overloads the [] subscript operator so s[i] returns the i-th mark for 0 <= i <= 4, while any other index prints an out-of-range message. Read the five marks and a list of query indices, applying s[idx] for each query.

Input Format:
Line 1: five integers (the marks).
Line 2: an integer K.
Line 3: K query indices.

Output Format:
For each query, one line: 'Score <i>: <value>' for a valid index, or 'Score <i>: Invalid index' otherwise.

Constraints:
0 <= each mark <= 100, 1 <= K <= 10, -5 <= each query index <= 10

questions.title: Scoreboard Banner Builder
questions.description:
A stadium scoreboard frames the team name with '=' characters. Read a word (a single word, no spaces) and an integer N, then print a banner: a line of N '=' characters, the word on its own line, and another line of N '=' characters.

Input Format:
One line with a word and an integer N separated by a space.

Output Format:
Line 1: N '=' characters
Line 2: the word
Line 3: N '=' characters
For sample input CHAMPIONS 6 the banner is:
======
CHAMPIONS
======

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 20, word length 1 to 15 (uppercase letters only)

questions.title: Scoreboard Updater
questions.description:
A quiz scoreboard adds a fixed bonus to every player's score. Read N scores and a bonus, walk a pointer across the scores adding the bonus to each one through the pointer, then print the updated list and the team total.

Input Format:
First line: N and bonus (two integers).
Second line: N scores.

Output Format:
Updated: <list of updated scores>
Team total: <sum of updated scores>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, 0 <= bonus <= 50, 0 <= each score <= 200

questions.title: Seat Booking Map
questions.description:
An auditorium seats visitors in a grid; each cell is 0 for available or 1 for booked. Read R and C, then the R*C seat states in row-major order. Print the seat map where every 0 becomes 'A' (available) and every 1 becomes 'B' (booked), one row per line with no spaces, then print how many seats are booked.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C values, each 0 or 1, in row-major order.

Output Format:
R lines of A/B characters (C characters per line, no spaces), then:
Booked: <number of 1s>

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, each value is 0 or 1
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= R, C <= 50, each value is 0 or 1

questions.title: Seating Chart Flip
questions.description:
An event coordinator stores a seating chart as a grid and the display software needs it flipped: rows must become columns. Read R and C, then the R*C chart values in row-major order, and print the transpose of the matrix.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
C lines; line j contains the values of column j of the original matrix separated by single spaces (the transpose has C rows and R columns).

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -100 <= element <= 100

questions.title: Section Score Merger
questions.description:
Two sections of a course wrote the same test and the coordinator stores both score grids with the same shape. Read R and C, then the R*C scores of section A, then the R*C scores of section B. Print the combined grid obtained by adding the two matrices cell by cell.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers (matrix A) in row-major order.
Then: R*C integers (matrix B) in row-major order.

Output Format:
R lines with the sum matrix, values separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -100 <= element <= 100

questions.title: Sensor Calibrator
questions.description:
A weather station calibrates raw sensor readings: any reading strictly below the threshold is doubled to amplify the weak signal, and readings at or above the threshold stay unchanged. Read N readings into a heap array created with new, walk a pointer through the array applying the rule, print the calibrated list, then release the memory with delete[].

Input Format:
First line: N and threshold (two integers).
Second line: N integer readings.

Output Format:
Calibrated: <list of N values separated by single spaces>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -100 <= threshold <= 100, -100 <= each reading <= 100

questions.title: Sensor Range Clamp Class
questions.description:
A weather station keeps sensor readings inside a safe range stored in the object. Define a class Sensor with private low, high and value fields, a setRange() setter, a setReading() member function that clamps any reading below low up to low and any reading above high down to high, and a getReading() getter. Read the range and three raw readings, then report the stored value after each setReading() call.

Input Format:
One line with five integers: low, high and three raw readings.

Output Format:
Reading 1: <stored value>
Reading 2: <stored value>
Reading 3: <stored value>

Constraints:
0 <= low <= high <= 1000, -100 <= each raw reading <= 2000

questions.title: Sensor Readings Report
questions.description:
A weather station logs N temperature readings for the day. Read N and then N integer readings into an array, then print the total of all readings and the average with exactly two decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N readings.

Output Format:
Total: <sum>
Average: <average with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= reading <= 100

questions.title: Sentence Length from File
questions.description:
A typing trainer stores a practice sentence in a file and reports its length by reading the file back. Read one sentence (a single line) and write it to sent20.txt. Then reopen the file, read the sentence back and print it together with its length.

Input Format:
One line of text (may contain spaces).

Output Format:
Stored: <sentence read from file>
Length: <length of the stored sentence>

Constraints:
1 <= sentence length <= 100

Length: 25

questions.title: Sentence Statistician
questions.description:
An editor plugin analyzes a sentence and reports word statistics. Read the whole line with getline. Words are separated by one or more spaces. Print the number of words, the longest word, the shortest word and the average word length with exactly two decimals. If several words tie for longest or shortest, report the earliest one.

Input Format:
One line containing a sentence with at least one word.

Output Format:
Words: <count>
Longest: <longest word>
Shortest: <shortest word>
Average: <average word length with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= sentence length <= 300, words are separated by one or more spaces

questions.title: Session Alive Counter
questions.description:
A cloud platform tracks overlapping user sessions with a live counter. Keep a plain global int alive initialized to 0. Define a class Session whose constructor increases alive by 1 and prints 'Session <name> started, alive: <alive>', and whose destructor decreases alive by 1 and prints 'Session <name> ended, alive: <alive>'. Read N and then N session tags. First create a long-running Session named main, then for each tag create a short-lived Session inside a block, print 'Working in <tag>' while it lives, and let it expire at the end of the block. After all sessions print 'All sessions closed, alive: 0'.

Input Format:
Tokens separated by spaces: N followed by N session tags (single words).

Output Format:
Session main started, alive: 1
For each session: Session <tag> started, alive: 2 / Working in <tag> / Session <tag> ended, alive: 1
All sessions closed, alive: 0

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 4; each tag is a single word of at most 10 characters

questions.title: Set Sorted Unique Collector
questions.description:
A hashtag tracker only cares about distinct tags. Read N integers into a set, then report how many unique values it holds and list them in ascending order — the set sorts and de-duplicates for you.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N integers (duplicates possible).

Output Format:
Unique: <number of distinct values>
Then each distinct value in ascending order, one per line.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -100000 <= value <= 100000

questions.title: Shape Area Through Abstract Base
questions.description:
Abstract classes define a contract without implementation. Shape declares a pure virtual area() = 0 and can never be created itself; Circle and Square inherit and each supply the real area formula. Read the shape code and its size, build the right object through a Shape pointer, and print the polymorphic area with two decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with a character (C for circle, S for square) and one number: the radius for C or the side for S.

Output Format:
Area: <value with exactly 2 decimals>

Constraints:
Code is C or S; 1 <= size <= 1000.
questions.inputconstrains: Code is C or S; 1 <= size <= 1000

questions.title: Shape Composer Total Area
questions.description:
A canvas composer assembles shapes from a build list and bills the whole canvas. Shape is abstract with pure virtual area() and name(); Circle and Square implement both. Read N shapes (C radius or S side), park them in an array of Shape pointers, then walk the list polymorphically printing each shape's name and area, and finish with the sum of all areas.

Input Format:
First line: N. Next N lines: a character (C or S) and a number (radius or side).

Output Format:
For each shape in input order: <Circle or Square> area: <value with 2 decimals>
Last line: Total area: <sum with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100; 1 <= size <= 1000.

questions.title: Shape vs Circle Describe Drill
questions.description:
Practice plain method overriding. Base class Shape has describe() printing 'I am a shape'. Derived class Circle redefines describe() to print 'I am a circle'. Read the picker and an item number, create the matching object directly, and call describe() on it.

Input Format:
One line with a character and an integer: the picker and the item number. 'C' creates a Circle; any other character creates a Shape.

Output Format:
Item <id>:
I am a circle   (when picker is C)
or
I am a shape    (otherwise)

Constraints:
1 <= item number <= 999.

questions.title: Shift Clock via Operator+
questions.description:
A shift scheduler adds two shift durations. Define a Time class with hours and minutes and overload the + operator to add two times with normalization: a minute total of 60 or more carries into hours. Print the combined duration as hh:mm.

Input Format:
One line with four integers: h1 m1 h2 m2 (each minutes value is below 60).

Output Format:
One line: '<h>:<mm>' where the minutes are shown as exactly two digits (zero padded) and the hours are printed as-is (they may exceed 24).

Constraints:
0 <= hours <= 48, 0 <= minutes <= 59

questions.title: Shop Receipt File Writer
questions.description:
A shop counter writes each purchased item into bill20.txt before totalling the bill. Read N and then N item-price pairs (item is a single word, price an integer). Store each pair on its own line, then reopen the file, print every line and the total of all prices.

Input Format:
First line: N. Then N lines, each with an item (single word) and an integer price.

Output Format:
One line per item: <item> : <price>
Then: Total: <sum of prices>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 10, 1 <= price <= 10000

questions.title: Shopping Cart Subtotal
questions.description:
An online store totals the items in a shopper's cart. Read N and then N integer item prices into an array, then print the subtotal by adding every price.

Input Format:
One line with N + 1 integers: N followed by the N item prices.

Output Format:
Subtotal: <sum> rupees

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= price <= 5000

questions.title: Shout It in Capitals

A notification banner must be loud. Read one word and print it converted to all uppercase letters. Lowercase letters become uppercase; other characters stay unchanged.

Input Format:
One line with one word.

Output Format:
Loud: <uppercase word>

1 <= word length <= 100, word contains letters and digits only

questions.title: Show Seat Booking Guard
questions.description:
A theatre box office guards seat booking with try-catch. Read the seats available and the seats requested. If the requested count exceeds the available seats, throw the requested count as an int; the catch(int) handler prints the failure line. Otherwise the booking is confirmed.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: available and requested.

Output Format:
Booking confirmed: <requested> seats
or:
Booking failed: requested <requested> seats

Constraints:
0 <= available <= 500, 0 <= requested <= 500

questions.title: Signal Fault Router
questions.description:
A device monitor routes numeric signal codes to typed fault handlers. Read a signal code. Inside one try block: code 1 throws the integer 100; code 2 throws the text disk failure; code 3 throws an unnamed double fault; any other code is healthy. Use three catch handlers written in order — catch(int), catch(const char*) and catch(...) — each printing its own line.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: signal code.

Output Format:
One line, depending on the code:
Integer fault: 100 (code 1)
Text fault: disk failure (code 2)
Unknown fault (code 3)
Signal <code>: all clear (any other code)

Constraints:
0 <= code <= 9

questions.title: Signboard Spiral Scan
questions.description:
A stadium signboard stores a grid of numbers and the controller scans them in spiral order: start at the top-left corner, move right across the top row, then down the rightmost column, then left across the bottom row, then up the leftmost column, and repeat inward until every cell has been visited. Read R and C, then the R*C values in row-major order, and print the spiral scan.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers in row-major order.

Output Format:
R*C lines, one visited element per line in spiral order.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -1000 <= element <= 1000

questions.title: Sliding Window Pointer Scanner
questions.description:
A network monitor scans traffic counts with a sliding window. Read N and the window size W, then N integers. Slide two pointers across the data: add the entering element through the front pointer and drop the leaving element through the rear pointer, printing the sum of every window as it forms. Finally print the maximum window sum seen.

Input Format:
First line: N and W (two integers, W <= N).
Second line: N integers.

Output Format:
Window sums: <s1> <s2> ... <s_last>
Max window sum: <m>

Constraints:
1 <= W <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= each value <= 10000

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
For each room i: Lamp on, then Room <i> visited, then Lamp off on three lines. After the last room: All rooms checked

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 5

questions.title: Stack on the Heap
questions.description:
A text editor keeps its undo history on a stack built over a heap array, using a pure pointer as the top marker (top points one slot past the top element). Read the number of commands C, then C commands, one per line: push x, pop, or peek. The stack starts empty. Every pop prints the removed value and every peek prints the top value, each on its own line; a pop or peek on an empty stack prints UNDERFLOW. After all commands, print the values still on the stack from top to bottom on one line prefixed with Stack from top:, or Stack from top: EMPTY when nothing remains. Release the heap array before exiting.

Input Format:
First line: one integer C.
Next C lines: one command each.

Output Format:
One line per pop/peek result, then the final stack line.

Constraints:
1 <= C <= 200, -1000 <= x <= 1000

A warehouse dashboard draws every stack of cartons as a row of box tokens. Read an integer N and print N rows; the top row shows N boxes and every row below has one box fewer. Each box is printed as the two-character token [] and boxes in a row are separated by a single space.

Input Format:
One line with one integer N.

Output Format:
N lines; displayed row r (1-based) has N - r + 1 box tokens separated by single spaces.
For sample input 4 the display is:
[] [] [] []
[] [] []
[] []
[]

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 15

questions.title: Warehouse Stock Comparison
questions.description:
A warehouse chain compares stock counts of the same products in two depots. Read R and C, then depot 1 counts, then depot 2 counts (same shape). Print the difference matrix depot1 - depot2 cell by cell; a negative value means depot 2 holds more of that product.

Input Format:
First line: R and C.
Then: R*C integers (depot 1) in row-major order.
Then: R*C integers (depot 2) in row-major order.

Output Format:
R lines with the difference matrix (depot1 - depot2), values separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 50, -100 <= element <= 100

questions.title: Washer Cycle Time Report

Output Format:

Minutes per cycle: <minutes>
Total wash time: <cycles * minutes> minutes

questions.title: Water Tank Alert System
questions.description:
An apartment water tank has a level sensor. Read the current level (integer litres) and the tank capacity (integer litres). Compute the fill percent using integer arithmetic: level * 100 / capacity. Use the conditional (ternary) operator to choose the alert text: REFILL NOW when the percent is below 20, otherwise LEVEL OK. Also compute the litres needed to fill the tank and the pump minutes, where the pump moves 50 litres per minute and a part-minute counts as a full minute (use the ternary operator for that rounding too).

Input Format:
One line with two integers: current level and capacity.

Output Format:
Level: <level>
Capacity: <capacity>
Percent: <level * 100 / capacity>
Status: <REFILL NOW or LEVEL OK>
Litres to fill: <capacity - level>
Pump minutes: <needed / 50, plus 1 more when needed % 50 is not 0>

Constraints:
0 <= level <= capacity <= 10000

Input Format:
First line: N. Next N lines: a character ('L' lion, 'E' elephant, 'M' monkey).

Output Format:

Elephant eats 20 kg of cane / Elephant trumpets happily
Monkey eats 2 kg of banana / Monkey chatters away
Then:
---- Feeding summary ----
Lions fed: <count>
Elephants fed: <count>
Monkeys fed: <count>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100.

mcqQuestions.Option1: ios::trunc keeps old content, ios::app erases it
mcqQuestions.Option2: ios::trunc erases existing content on open, ios::app preserves it and writes at the end
mcqQuestions.Option3: Both behave identically on existing files
mcqQuestions.Option4: ios::app erases content when the file already exists

mcqQuestions.title: while Condition Timing
mcqQuestions.description: In a while loop, when is the condition evaluated?
mcqQuestions.Option2: Before every iteration, including the first
mcqQuestions.Option3: After every iteration, but not before the first
mcqQuestions.Option4: Only when break or continue is used
